red.rationale: Stearates coat particles and reduce bioavailability.
Animal gelatin carries a documented glyphosate-contamination concern (Seneff) and is non-vegetarian.
Dicalcium phosphate is a poorly-chosen filler that Glen avoids.
Titanium dioxide is a whitening agent with no nutritional purpose and safety concerns.
Synthetic dyes have no nutritional purpose.
Glen 2026-10-08: an enteric capsule that is not phthalate-free fails. Shellac is not covered by this ruling. "CAP" is not an alias: it would match "veggie cap".

Glen 2026-10-08: an enteric capsule whose label does not say phthalate-free fails until the maker confirms it. Confirm with the maker. Glen's figure, no source recorded: about 80% of enteric capsules use phthalates. DRcaps (hypromellose and gellan gum) are phthalate-free.

yellow.rationale: Silica as a flow-agent filler is inert and tolerated, but not ideal; it counts against a product only as a filler, never when present as an intentional nutrient.
